chunks: If a man strikes a man with a stick or with a rock, and he dies from a single blow before he speaks, then it is quasi-intentional killing (shubh al-'amd), and the blood money (diya) is upon the killer.
And if he pounces upon him and hits him incessantly with the stick or with rocks until he kills him, then it is deliberate intentional killing ('amd) for which he shall be killed (in retaliation).
And if he strikes him with a single blow, and he speaks (after), then remains alive for a day or more than a day, then dies — then it is quasi-intentional killing.

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: Diya — blood money, a financial compensation paid to the victim's family in cases of quasi-intentional or accidental killing
key_terms.شِبْهُ الْعَمْدِ: Quasi-intentional killing — a legal category between accident and premeditated murder, carrying diya but not qisas
key_terms.عَمْدٌ: Intentional/'amd — deliberate premeditated murder, carrying the penalty of qisas (retaliation)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between intentional killing ('amd) and quasi-intentional killing (shubh al-'amd) in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delineates the Islamic jurisprudential categories of homicide by weapon according to circumstances. The first and third scenarios — a single blow where death follows immediately without speech, or a single blow followed by survival and speech before eventual death — both constitute quasi-intentional killing (shubh al-'amd), which requires the payment of blood money (diya) by the killer. The intermediate scenario — repeated incessant blows until death — constitutes fully intentional murder ('amd), for which the killer faces execution by retaliation (qisas). This hadith is foundational in Shia fiqh for establishing the criteria distinguishing 'amd from shubh al-'amd.
